v.rationale:
All three pass their own tests. All three wrap the reply insert and counter increment in a transaction and send each mention as a separate private Mail::to() plus one database notification, only after the commit. My probes confirmed that a failing counter update rolls back the reply and sends nothing. The differences are in how usernames are matched and in code idioms.

impl-1 (rank 1) has the cleanest code: the relation `associate()`, tight fillable, multibyte-safe lowercasing, and a `/u` regex that resolves `@josé` correctly. It also has the strongest tests, including multibyte length and a mail-render check. Its one real bug is that the regex stops at dots, while its own factory generates dotted usernames. So `@john.doe` notifies `john` and skips `john.doe`.

impl-2 (rank 2) is nearly the same code. It has the same dotted-username bug, adds a second one (no `/u` flag, so `@josé` notifies `jos`), and wraps the logic in an extra single-use Action class.

impl-3 (rank 3) handles dotted usernames correctly. However, its lowercasing is not multibyte-safe (it stored `Émile`), its matching is ASCII-only (`@josé` notifies `jos`), and it has weaker idioms: `reply_count` and the foreign keys are mass-assignable, the dispatch logic sits in the controller, it uses plain arrays instead of collections, and it keeps unused Queueable/SerializesModels traits. impl-2 and impl-3 are close. impl-2 ranks higher on cleaner Eloquent and collection idioms and on tests.
